prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a steep gradient across a rough plastered wall on the left and upper-left, ranging from roughly 0.2–0.3 metres at the bright upper-left corner to about 1.5–2.0 metres toward the lower-right edge, while the floor and scaffolding drop below to the right appear completely dark at roughly 2–4 metres below the camera wearer. Within arm's reach (0.3–0.7 metres in front and below the viewpoint), the camera wearer's right hand and forearm hold a plastering float against the wall, and the wearer's feet and bamboo scaffolding poles are visible in the lower-right corner at about 1.0–1.5 metres away. Across the 5 frames, the hand and tool move from the lower-left in frame 1 (0.3 metres) upward and slightly right along the wall in frames 2–4 (0.4–0.5 metres), then extend further away to about 0.6–0.7 metres in frame 5. The map clarifies the continuous 3D receding plane of the wall and the distinct foreground separation of the scaffolding bars in frames 2–4 better than the flatly lit RGB image, where shadows and uniform grey texture obscure depth cues. However, the depth map is unreliable where the plastering tool blends smoothly into the wall surface in frames 2–5 and in the overexposed background on the far right, which collapses into uniform black with lost floor detail.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map is completely blank across frames 1 to 4, failing to detect the camera wearer's hand, arm, plastering tool, feet, or the surrounding wall and scaffolding. Only in frame 5 does it detect the camera wearer's extended right forearm and hand at the bottom-center (roughly 0.5–0.7 metres away, labeled 'person' in pink) and a small portion of the lower body or foot in the bottom-right corner (roughly 1.0–1.2 metres away, in brown), both extending from the bottom edge of the frame where the rest of the camera wearer's body is out of view. No other people are present in the scene, though a tiny silhouette at the far right edge of frame 5 is ignored, and the camera wearer's gaze remains directed downward and forward toward the wall within arm's reach. When present in frame 5, the mask sharply isolates the boundary of the bare forearm and hand against the similarly toned grey wall and shadow, which is harder to separate at a glance in the RGB frame. Overall, this map is highly unreliable because it misses the camera wearer's limbs in the first four frames entirely and never segments the handheld float, the wall, or the scaffolding.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects only a magenta right-hand skeleton in the lower-center of frames 3 and 4, positioned roughly 0.3–0.4 metres in front of and below the camera wearer's viewpoint within immediate arm's reach, while frames 1, 2, and 5 are completely black. In both detected frames, the hand is oriented palm-forward against the wall with the thumb on the left and four fingers angled upward and slightly right gripping the handle of the plastering float, which partially occludes the fingertips in RGB. Between frame 3 and frame 4, the hand skeleton stays at roughly the same height and distance while shifting slightly to the right and spreading its fingers marginally as the arm moves along the wall surface. This map reveals the precise 3D articulation of the thumb, palm base, and individual finger joints inside the deep shadow cast by the float in frames 3 and 4, which are dark and motion-blurred in the RGB strip. However, the map is unreliable across the sequence because it completely misses the hand when it is partially cut off at the bottom-left in frame 1 or further away in frames 2 and 5, and it fails to render any yellow body or arm keypoints for the camera wearer.
